currentContext.strengths: India's largest residential developer by booking value for the 3rd consecutive year; booking value CAGR of 41% over the past 3 years|Large, geographically diversified execution track record — delivered ~78 million sq. ft. since FY 2018, ~12.1 million sq. ft. in FY 2025-26 alone|Strong brand trust and customer experience — Net Promoter Score of 71%, with buyer preference in the sector consolidating around large, established, trusted developers|Record business development momentum — added projects with cumulative expected booking value of ~₹1,22,000 crore over the last 4 years, sustaining a large forward launch pipeline|Technology-led execution — VIRA digital labour platform for real-time workforce tracking/incentive payments, digital sales platform, and AI-assisted design/layout optimisation|Sector-leading ESG/sustainability recognition (S&P CSA #1 globally, GRESB #1 globally, CDP 'A' ratings) supporting access to capital and premium positioning
currentContext.strategies: Strengthen profitability through disciplined capital allocation|Enhance customer experience by delivering best-in-class quality and design|Accelerate adoption of digital technologies across development and customer-facing operations|Continue premiumisation focus — larger homes, superior specifications, lifestyle-oriented communities|Selective, disciplined land acquisition/business development in markets with strong demand visibility, without stretching the balance sheet|Grow and diversify the project pipeline across 15+ cities, leveraging scale and execution track record|Benefit from sector consolidation by partnering with or gaining share from smaller, undercapitalised developers via strong governance and delivery track record|The Board recommended a dividend for FY 2025-26 (₹10 per equity share, 200% of face value), subject to Members' approval at the 41st AGM. Related-party transactions were conducted in the ordinary course of business on an arm's-length basis with prior Audit Committee approval, and no material RPTs required separate Member approval during the year. Separately, the AGM notice seeks Member ratification/waiver of managerial remuneration paid to the Executive Chairperson in excess of Companies Act limits (due to inadequate standalone profits), indicating remuneration governance is closely tied to the Company's profit-computation framework rather than a stated reinvestment/leverage philosophy in this bundle.
currentContext.expansion: The routed text contains no named, project-specific capex or capacity-expansion plan for Godrej Properties itself (e.g. a new plant, facility or site with a commissioning timeline) — consistent with an asset-light residential/commercial developer whose growth is expressed through project/land additions rather than fixed-asset capacity. BRSR discloses that capital expenditure directed toward technologies improving environmental and social impact rose to 3% of total capex in FY 2025-26 from 0.6% in FY 2024-25, alongside R&D spend of 50% (FY26) / 50.75% (FY25) directed to such technologies, and sustainable procurement of over 95% across sites (within 400km, per IGBC local-procurement guidelines). A capital commitments disclosure (capital work-in-progress and investment property under construction, net of advances) is referenced for the years ended March 31, 2026 and March 31, 2025, but the source table did not print a currency unit, so the figure is not usable here (see capex_disclosed). Broader sector-level capex catalysts referenced (not Godrej-specific projects) include the Union Budget 2026-27's infrastructure-led public capex push (Metro Phase III, new High-Speed Rail corridors), the introduction of City Economic Regions (CERs) to open real estate growth in Tier-II/III cities, and continued GCC-driven office-space absorption growth.

risks.risk: Geographic concentration of the portfolio, with physical/climate exposure concentrated in the coastal and high-rainfall markets
risks.note: The risk-management chapter states GPL assesses each risk for 'geographic concentration, recognising that exposure varies across our markets', and flags that 'physical risks such as flooding carry higher likelihood in coastal and high-rainfall geographies'. The company runs four zonal P&Ls (MMR, NCR, West & East, South, each with its own Zonal CEO), so a weather or demand shock in one metro cluster hits a large share of deliveries rather than being diversified away.

risks.risk: Regulatory divergence across state jurisdictions on land use, taxation and construction norms
risks.note: The AR states plainly that 'regulatory risk differs across state jurisdictions as land use, taxation, and construction norms evolve unevenly'. For a developer operating across MMR, NCR, West/East and South simultaneously, this means approvals, cost of compliance and launch timing are set by four separate and unsynchronised policy regimes; a single adverse state rule change can strand an approved project pipeline in that zone.

risks.risk: Dependence on continued land-bank replenishment and on brand equity as the primary competitive assets
risks.note: ERM objective 04 defines the job as strengthening 'the business's capacity to recognise the most important resources and put strategies in place to protect and strengthen land bank, brand equity, contractor ecosystem, and talent' — the company's own ranking of what it cannot afford to lose. For an asset-light, JV- and outright-purchase-driven model, business development (land access at an acceptable price) is the binding constraint on future booking value, and the brand is what makes the JV partner choose GPL over a rival.

risks.risk: Execution is outsourced: dependence on the contractor ecosystem, with unresolved value-chain grievances at project level
risks.note: Contractors are named among the four critical resources GPL must 'protect and strengthen', and the OH&S material issue explicitly extends its duty of care to 'employees, contractors, and tenants'. The BRSR grievance register shows 6 Value Chain Partner complaints filed in FY 2025-26 with 5 still open at year end, which the company says have 'been escalated to senior operational leadership as per internal protocols'. Contractor capacity and disputes sit directly on the delivery schedule, which is where a developer's revenue recognition lives.

risks.risk: Post-handover customer disputes and society/conveyance liabilities at delivered projects
risks.note: 15 customer complaints were filed in FY 2025-26 with 7 still pending at close, and the AR names them: Godrej Nest, Mumbai, where the dispute is over 'society formation and conveyance deed execution' plus dissatisfaction with the Facilities Management Agency; and Godrej Frontier, NCR, where a resident dispute over constructing a temple inside the society has required GPL to seek 'an intervention from the Department of Town and Country Planning (DTCP)'. These are named, live obligations that outlast the sale and can draw the developer into regulator-mediated proceedings.

risks.risk: Cybersecurity incidents and supply-chain shocks as identified business-continuity threats
risks.note: ERM objective 05 requires response and recovery plans for disruptions 'arising from supply-chain shocks, extreme weather events, and cybersecurity incidents', and the Risk Management Committee charter mandates a framework covering 'information, cyber security risks' alongside financial, operational and sectoral risk. Both sit in the company's own charter language rather than in a generic risk list, and a construction supply-chain shock transmits straight into input cost and completion dates.

risks.risk: Occupational health and safety exposure across construction, property management and maintenance activity
risks.note: The BRSR material-issues register classifies OH&S as a Risk with negative financial implications, tying it to 'financial risks related to workplace injuries, liability claims, and potential fines' and to compliance with safety regulation as a legal obligation. Mitigation rests on an OH&S management system 'aligned with ISO 45001: 2018' with audits and risk assessments — a control, not an elimination, given the number of active sites and third-party workers.

Talent is the fourth of the four resources ERM objective 04 commits to protecting, and the FY 2025-26 senior management table itself shows churn at the top: Mr. Sandeep Navlakhe was appointed Chief Operations Officer from August 01, 2025 in place of Mr. Vikas Singhal, with further changes footnoted against the Chief Sales/Marketing, Zonal CEO West & East and Zonal CEO MMR roles. In a business where land sourcing and zonal execution are relationship-led, senior departures carry pipeline risk.

one-line thesis: GPL delivered record FY26 bookings (INR 34,171 cr) and collections (INR 19,965 cr), signaling a shift from hyper-growth land banking to steady 20% execution-led growth with emerging free cash flow positivity. While geopolitical tensions pose a manageable 5-6% cost headwind, the robust launch pipeline and dividend initiation confirm balance sheet strength and a maturing capital allocation cycle.
financial scorecard: Revenue: INR 3,895 cr (+47% YoY); EBITDA: INR 959 cr (+51% YoY, margin ~24.6%); PAT: INR 650 cr (+70% YoY); Order Book (Bookings): INR 10,163 cr (Q4), INR 34,171 cr (FY26, +16% YoY); Net Debt: Comfortable range, trending towards FCF positive by FY28. One-offs: JV dilution in Bangalore project reduced consolidated economic interest from 93% to 88%, slightly pressuring imputed margins.
guidance: Revenue Growth: Implicitly strong via 20% booking growth target; Margin: Stable 10-15% PAT range; Order Inflow: >INR 39,000 cr (FY27E, +20% YoY); Capex/Commissioning: Construction spend to grow double-digits YoY to secure OC for FY28 deliveries.
order book & pipeline: FY26 Bookings: INR 34,171 cr (105% of guidance); Q4 Bookings: INR 10,163 cr (21% QoQ); Portfolio Addition (GDV): INR 42,100 cr (+59% YoY, 200% of guidance); Inventory available for sale up 35% YoY.
segment / subsidiary detail: Geography: Mumbai (>INR 10k cr), Bengaluru (INR 8,801 cr), NCR (INR 7,412 cr), Pune (INR 3,659 cr), Hyderabad (INR 2,360 cr). Product: 11 projects crossed INR 1,000 cr sales each. Mix: 60% New Launches, 40% Sustenance.
growth verticals / optionality: Launch pipeline includes Godrej Golf Links (NCR), Bandra tower (Mumbai), Vikhroli land parcel, and Thane acquisition (INR 7,500 cr GDV). Expansion into new markets like Calcutta group housing and plotted developments in Coimbatore.
margins & cost dynamics: Imputed EBIT margin ~24.5% (slight dip due to JV mix). Geopolitical conflict estimated to impact input costs by 5-6% max, translating to 0.1-0.2% margin erosion per quarter; manageable via price hikes and forward contracts.
capex / expansion: Construction spend jumped 62% in FY26 to enable future deliveries. FY27 spend expected to grow double-digits. Pending land payments for FY26 deals: ~INR 1,500 cr.
capital allocation: Initiated dividend payout signaling consistent FCF generation outlook. Share buyback (5% stake) executed in FY26. Targeting ROE of 20% by FY28. BD spend intensity expected to normalize as % of sales.
risks & watch-items: Geopolitical escalation prolonging input cost inflation; Delay in NCR project approvals (Ashok Vihar, Gurgaon); Potential AI/IT sector slowdown impacting Bengaluru/Pune demand sentiment; Execution slippages on aggressive launch calendar.
management quality / tone: Confident yet cautious; Emphasizes 'cautious optimism' regarding global uncertainty; Focus shifting from land banking to execution and cash generation; Transparent on cost headwinds.
non-obvious takeaways: Management explicitly frames the 20% guidance growth as 'moderate' only because FY26 actuals missed an internal INR 1,000 cr target due to March chaos; implies underlying run-rate is higher. The 1% payment plan is clarified as a marketing/sourcing tool (similar to auto leases) rather than a true deferred payment structure, benchmarked to CLP for cash flow planning.

themes.title: Real-estate up-cycle - premium housing & redevelopment
themes.need: The residential up-cycle is now presales-led with a visible margin cost. SOBHA posted its highest-ever presales at INR 3,656cr (+76% YoY, 2.34 msf at an average INR 15,655/sqft, NCR at a record INR 1,384cr) and guided FY27 presales at +30% or better - but reported EBITDA is still only ~9.7%, guided to 17-20% only by exit-Q4, and forthcoming-project marginal cash flow was cut from ~INR 86bn to INR 68.3bn on a heavier joint-development mix. SUNTECK booked INR 787cr of presales (+20%) with ZERO launches in the quarter, with aspirational-luxury (Naigaon/Kalyan) at 21% of presales 'picking up because of the lower interest rate' - the first sign the rate-elastic end is turning on demand rather than inventory release. DLF's FY26 bookings of INR20,143cr and 50mn sq ft of rental at 95% occupancy anchor the annuity leg; LODHA/GODREJPROP/PRESTIGE-tier and MMR redevelopers (RUSTOMJEE, KALPATARU, RAYMONDREL, MANINFRA, SURAJEST) ride premiumization; PHOENIXLTD/EMBDL on mixed-use.
themes.driver: SOBHA's exit-Q4 margin ramp from ~9.7% to 17-20% is the falsifiable claim (JD-heavy growth structurally lowers marginal margins); rate-elastic aspirational absorption (SUNTECK); FY27 launch-pipeline execution and festive booking momentum.

order_book.title: Order book & pipeline
order_book.body: FY26 Bookings: INR 34,171 cr (105% of guidance); Q4 Bookings: INR 10,163 cr (21% QoQ); Portfolio Addition (GDV): INR 42,100 cr (+59% YoY, 200% of guidance); Inventory available for sale up 35% YoY.

guidance.title: Guidance
guidance.body: Revenue Growth: Implicitly strong via 20% booking growth target; Margin: Stable 10-15% PAT range; Order Inflow: >INR 39,000 cr (FY27E, +20% YoY); Capex/Commissioning: Construction spend to grow double-digits YoY to secure OC for FY28 deliveries.

growth_optionality.title: Growth verticals / optionality
growth_optionality.body: Launch pipeline includes Godrej Golf Links (NCR), Bandra tower (Mumbai), Vikhroli land parcel, and Thane acquisition (INR 7,500 cr GDV). Expansion into new markets like Calcutta group housing and plotted developments in Coimbatore.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Indian residential real estate sector sustaining its post-pandemic structural upcycle, supported by domestic macroeconomic fundamentals, a stable policy environment and continued income growth in mid/high-income brackets
- RBI's cumulative 125 bps repo rate cut since February 2025 has improved housing affordability and eased financing conditions, catalysing end-user demand
- Pronounced premiumisation shift: homes priced above ₹10 million now constitute 50% of total annual industry sales, even as overall volumes across the top 8 cities moderated ~1% YoY to ~3.48 lakh units in 2025
- Consolidation within residential real estate continues to benefit large, organised, brand-led developers as buyer preference shifts toward credible developers with demonstrated delivery track records
- Union Budget 2026-27 raised public capital expenditure to ₹12.2 lakh crore (a 9% YoY increase) and rationalised income tax, supporting aspirational housing demand, even as PMAY-Urban allocation was moderated 5.9% YoY to ₹18,625 crore
- Urbanisation, rising per-capita disposable income and a shift in income distribution from a 'pyramid to a diamond' shape support long-term structural demand for residential real estate
- Office market: GCCs are now the dominant occupier segment (38% of CY2025 transactions, the highest share on record) with 44% share of Q1 2026 absorption, driving office leasing towards a 100 million sq. ft. annual milestone within two years
- Climate/ESG has become a baseline occupier requirement in office real estate — green-certified assets captured 75-93% of Q4 2025 leasing/new completions — creating obsolescence risk for non-ESG assets and a retrofit/asset-modernisation opportunity
- Government's introduction of City Economic Regions (CERs) is expected to unlock real estate demand in Tier-II/III cities beyond saturated metros
- CPSE asset recycling through dedicated REITs is expected to deepen India's real estate investment landscape
- Diversified and growing project pipeline spanning 15+ cities, underpinned by a demonstrated track record of execution at scale
- FY 2025-26 was the best-ever year for business development: 18 new projects added with saleable potential of ~33 million sq. ft. and expected booking value of ₹42,100 crore, spread across 11 markets (including new markets Panipat, Coimbatore, Raipur and Vadodara)
- 4th consecutive year of adding projects with expected booking value over ₹20,000 crore; cumulative expected booking value of ~₹1,22,000 crore added over the last 4 years
- 38 new projects and phases launched in FY 2025-26 across 9 cities

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: Imputed EBIT margin ~24.5% (slight dip due to JV mix). Geopolitical conflict estimated to impact input costs by 5-6% max, translating to 0.1-0.2% margin erosion per quarter; manageable via price hikes and forward contracts.

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: Initiated dividend payout signaling consistent FCF generation outlook. Share buyback (5% stake) executed in FY26. Targeting ROE of 20% by FY28. BD spend intensity expected to normalize as % of sales.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: The routed text contains no named, project-specific capex or capacity-expansion plan for Godrej Properties itself (e.g. a new plant, facility or site with a commissioning timeline) — consistent with an asset-light residential/commercial developer whose growth is expressed through project/land additions rather than fixed-asset capacity. BRSR discloses that capital expenditure directed toward technologies improving environmental and social impact rose to 3% of total capex in FY 2025-26 from 0.6% in FY 2024-25, alongside R&D spend of 50% (FY26) / 50.75% (FY25) directed to such technologies, and sustainable procurement of over 95% across sites (within 400km, per IGBC local-procurement guidelines). A capital commitments disclosure (capital work-in-progress and investment property under construction, net of advances) is referenced for the years ended March 31, 2026 and March 31, 2025, but the source table did not print a currency unit, so the figure is not usable here (see capex_disclosed). Broader sector-level capex catalysts referenced (not Godrej-specific projects) include the Union Budget 2026-27's infrastructure-led public capex push (Metro Phase III, new High-Speed Rail corridors), the introduction of City Economic Regions (CERs) to open real estate growth in Tier-II/III cities, and continued GCC-driven office-space absorption growth.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Confident yet cautious; Emphasizes 'cautious optimism' regarding global uncertainty; Focus shifting from land banking to execution and cash generation; Transparent on cost headwinds.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- India's largest residential developer by booking value for the 3rd consecutive year; booking value CAGR of 41% over the past 3 years
- Large, geographically diversified execution track record — delivered ~78 million sq. ft. since FY 2018, ~12.1 million sq. ft. in FY 2025-26 alone
- Strong brand trust and customer experience — Net Promoter Score of 71%, with buyer preference in the sector consolidating around large, established, trusted developers
- Record business development momentum — added projects with cumulative expected booking value of ~₹1,22,000 crore over the last 4 years, sustaining a large forward launch pipeline
- Technology-led execution — VIRA digital labour platform for real-time workforce tracking/incentive payments, digital sales platform, and AI-assisted design/layout optimisation
- Sector-leading ESG/sustainability recognition (S&P CSA #1 globally, GRESB #1 globally, CDP 'A' ratings) supporting access to capital and premium positioning

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: Geopolitical escalation prolonging input cost inflation; Delay in NCR project approvals (Ashok Vihar, Gurgaon); Potential AI/IT sector slowdown impacting Bengaluru/Pune demand sentiment; Execution slippages on aggressive launch calendar.

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: Management explicitly frames the 20% guidance growth as 'moderate' only because FY26 actuals missed an internal INR 1,000 cr target due to March chaos; implies underlying run-rate is higher. The 1% payment plan is clarified as a marketing/sourcing tool (similar to auto leases) rather than a true deferred payment structure, benchmarked to CLP for cash flow planning.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Strengthen profitability through disciplined capital allocation
- Enhance customer experience by delivering best-in-class quality and design
- Accelerate adoption of digital technologies across development and customer-facing operations
- Continue premiumisation focus — larger homes, superior specifications, lifestyle-oriented communities
- Selective, disciplined land acquisition/business development in markets with strong demand visibility, without stretching the balance sheet
- Grow and diversify the project pipeline across 15+ cities, leveraging scale and execution track record
- Benefit from sector …

challenges.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers
challenges.body:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Input cost inflation (tiles, marble) due to Middle East conflict | Small unlisted local contractors | loser | Med | Lack forward contracts and pricing power to pass on 5-6% cost increases compared to GPL. |
| Shift of investment demand from Dubai/UAE back to India due to geopolitical instability | Godrej Properties Ltd | beneficiary | High | Management cites 'silver lining' of fence-sitters returning to Indian premium real estate markets. |
| Margin compression from sustained high construction costs | Mid-tier listed peers with weak balance sheets | loser | Med | Peers unable to absorb 0.1-0.2% quarterly margin hit or access credit for working capital may lose market share. |

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Group] Presented as part of the Godrej Industries Group - 'Crafting tomorrow since 1897', $7 billion in annual sales, group companies' combined market cap over $20 billion, with real estate the group's largest business by sales.
- [Stock performance] Deck's value-creation slide claims a 16-year CAGR in stock price of 13.5% for Godrej Properties (INR 1 invested in Jan 2010 now worth 8.12) versus BSE Sensex 9.3% (4.36) and BSE Realty 3.2% (1.67), i.e. an IPO investment worth ~5X an identical investment in the BSE Realty Index.
- [Awards] 500+ awards received in the last 5 years; Golden Peacock National Quality Award 2026 received in Q1 FY27.
- [Delivery risk disclaimer] The FY28 BV recognition target is explicitly conditioned: 'Deliveries are dependent on receipt of regulatory approvals and can be delayed beyond initial expectations', with revenue recognition varying by project completion, business model, economic interest and accounting method.
- [Scope change] Saleable area was increased in several projects (Godrej Samaris and Sector-63A from 1.70 msf and 1.65 msf) and changed in Godrej MSR City, Vanatara, Woodscapes, Regal Pavilion and Brooklyn Avenue on account of changes in project scope or design efficiency.
